 Judgment

1 By this judgment I will dispose of appeal u/sec.374 Cr.PC. filed on behalf of convict Rakesh Goyal @ Joginder Goyal against the judgment dated 14.05.2016 and order on sentence dated 16.05.2016 p a s s e d b y S h .
A s h u G a r g , L d . A C M M - I I , P a t i a l a  Rakesh Goyal @ Joginder Goyal Vs.
State House Court, New Delhi.
2 The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s Goel Store, E-418, New Ashok Nagar, Delhi-110096.
On 23.03.2009 at about 7.30 p.m. Food Inspector Sh. V. P. S. Chaudhary visited the said place and purchased 1500 grams of "Dal Moth" (ready for sale) from accused.
FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. Radha Charan.
The said Moth Dal was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act.
The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA.
Panchanama was prepared.
One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst.
As per the report of Analyst, sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz. Tartrazine."

R/O E-427 vs Food Inspector on 2 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57493807/
1 3
As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 23.11.2009 with the court.
Accused was summoned.
He has exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act to get the sample analyzed by CFL.

CFL reported "I am of the opinion that the sample does not conform to the standards of "Any other food grains" as per PFA Rules 1955 (Synthetic colour Tartrazine detected)."
 Rakesh Goyal @ Joginder Goyal Vs. State 4

was framed against accused u/sec.2 (a) (j) &
(m) read with sec.7 of PFA Act, 1954 punishable u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act.

After trial, vide judgment dated 14.05.2016 accused was convicted for offence u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act and vide order on sentence dated 16.05.2016, accused was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 2 years and fine of Rs.30,000/- and in default of payment of fine SI of 1 month.

6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:-
(i) There is variation in PA and CFL Report.
(ii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e. the bottles, jhawa, polythene were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official.
(iii) Chromatography test is not a reliable test.
7 No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
8 I have gone through the record, Trial Court record and have heard the submissions of Ld. counsel for appellant and Ld. SPP for State.
9 It is stated that there is variation in the report of PA and CFL and due to that reason benefit goes in favour of the accused.
Rakesh Goyal @ Joginder Goyal Vs. State

sentences.text: This line of argument was done before the trial court and was dealt in para 13 to 43 of the judgment.
I do not want to differ from the reasoning given by the trial court and thus the same is upheld.

10 It is further argued that both the scientists that Public Analyst as well as at CFL had used to detect colour by way of Paper Chromatography Test and the same is not a reliable test for detecting colour in food articles.
This leg of arguments was also done before the trial court and are being dealt by it in para 50 and 51.

I do not find any other opinion than that given by the trial court and thus the arguments addressed by Ld. counsel for appellant in this regard are rejected and the reasoning given by the R/O E-427 vs Food Inspector on 2 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57493807/
2 trial court is upheld.
11 It is further argued that compliance u/sec.14 PFA Rules was not proved on record by the prosecution.
It is stated that witnesses are deposing differently with respect to the cleanliness of jhaba etc.
It is further stated that it was the duty of the prosecution to prove these facts.
These arguments were also addressed before the trial court.
The relevant part of the judgment dealing with these arguments are in para 53 of the judgment.
12 As far as the arguments in this regard is concerned, the law discussed by the trial court is correct and the same is self explanatory.
However, as far as the analysis of facts are  Rakesh Goyal @ Joginder Goyal Vs. State concerned, to my opinion, the same requires some more elaboration.

sentences.text: 13 As far as Rule 14 of PFA Rules are concerned, it spells out that the FI shall use dry bottles or containers for the purposes of sampling.

However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry implements in sampling the articles of food.

entities.text: Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis.
So, the Hon. Supreme Court use the word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers".
Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559, it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in other judgments, like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean.

sentences.text: 14 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court is that if in evidence, the prosecution states that if the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement", it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample.
However, it is not the law that the FI shall spell out on which surfaces the sample commodity had touched while sampling.
However, if he chooses to spell out the implements/surfaces with which the sample commodity came into contact/touch, the same must be proved as clean and dry.
15 In the present case, the PW2/FI Radha Charan, SDM/LHA deposed in his cross-examination dated 17.07.2014 that "the Dal was weighed by putting it in the pan balance directly".
Similarly, PW3 Sh. Jagdish Prasad, FA/witness, deposed in his cross-examination dated 17.11.2014 that "FI weighted Moth Dal after putting into white colour polythene bag".

3
Now this is a contradiction.
However, none of the witnesses have deposed that the pan balance or the white polythene bag was clean and without any colour.

17 So, in these circumstances, the judgment and order on sentence of the trial court is reversed.
18 Accused Rakesh Goyal @ Joginder Goyal is acquitted of the charges u/sec.16(1A) read with sec.7 of PFA Act.
